extracted.intended_audience: public housing authorities (PHAs), Section 8 owners/administrators, and program participants (tenants/applicants)
extracted.subtask_short: HUD public housing and Section 8 rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements governing income/asset calculation, eligibility, rent and utility rules, owner selection preferences, and reexamination procedures for HUD public housing and Section 8 programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified welfare benefit reduction — definition and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: A specified welfare benefit reduction is (1) a reduction of welfare benefits by the welfare agency, in whole or in part, for a family member because of fraud by a family member in connection with the welfare program; or because of a welfare agency sanction against a family member for noncompliance with a welfare agency requirement to participate in an economic self-sufficiency program. It does not include reductions due to (i) expiration of a lifetime or other time limit on benefits; (ii) inability to obtain employment despite complying with work requirements; or (iii) noncompliance with other welfare agency requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original regulatory text enumerates what counts and explicitly excludes three categories of reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imputed welfare income — inclusion and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: A family's annual income includes imputed welfare income resulting from a specified welfare benefits reduction (as specified in notice to the PHA by the welfare agency), plus other annual income per §5.609.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHA may request welfare agency to inform in writing of amount, term, and reason for reduction; use that information to determine imputed welfare income at interim or regular reexamination; imputed income applies during the term of the reduction as specified by welfare agency notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offset for subsequent additional income against imputed welfare income
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of the imputed welfare income is offset by any additional income the family receives that commences after the sanction was imposed; when additional income from other sources equals or exceeds imputed welfare income, the imputed amount is reduced to zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHA must account for post-sanction income increases in calculating imputed welfare income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on including imputed welfare income for non-assisted families
rubrics_metrics.description: The PHA may not include imputed welfare income in annual income if the family was not an assisted resident at the time the sanction was imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHA must verify assisted status at time of sanction before including imputed welfare income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of PHA determination on imputed welfare income — tenant rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Public housing tenants who dispute the PHA calculation may request a grievance hearing under part 966, subpart B; Section 8 participants may request an informal hearing under §982.555. If the PHA denies modification, it must give written notice with brief explanation and state right to hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tenant is not required to pay an escrow deposit under §966.55(e) to obtain a grievance hearing for the portion of rent attributable to imputed welfare income.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHA reliance on welfare agency determinations and limits on PHA responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The PHA is responsible for determining the amount of imputed welfare income based on the welfare agency's notice, but is not responsible for determining whether the welfare agency's reduction was correctly determined; welfare agency determinations are subject to the welfare agency's appeal procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHA may rely on welfare agency notices and should direct families to the welfare agency for appeals of welfare determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of disallowance of earned income for persons with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The disallowance (exclusion) of earned income provided in §5.617 applies only to specified programs: HOME (24 CFR part 92); HOPWA (24 CFR part 574); Supportive Housing Program (24 CFR part 583); and the Housing Choice Voucher Program (24 CFR part 982).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation limits the program scope for the earned income disallowance benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for disallowance of earned income provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Key definitions: Baseline income = annual income immediately prior to implementation; Disallowance = exclusion from annual income; Previously unemployed = earned no more than 10 hours/week for 50 weeks at minimum wage in prior 12 months; Qualified family = family residing in or receiving tenant-based rental assistance under programs listed in paragraph (a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These defined terms are used to determine eligibility and calculation of the disallowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified family eligibility for disallowance
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualified family for disallowance is one whose annual income increases because (1) a family member with disabilities was previously unemployed for one or more years prior to employment; (2) increased earnings during participation in any economic self-sufficiency or job training program; or (3) new employment or increased earnings during or within six months after receiving assistance/benefits under TANF/WTW (with specified conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TANF benefit inclusion is not limited to monthly maintenance and may include one-time payments or wage subsidies provided total over six months is at least $500; responsible entity consults local TANF/WTW agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial 12-month exclusion of increased earnings for persons with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: During the 12 months beginning on the date a person with disabilities of a qualified family is first employed (or family first experiences income increase attributable to employment), the responsible entity must exclude from annual income any increase in income of that family member over prior income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a full exclusion for the initial 12-month period as defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second 12-month exclusion and phase-in (50% exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 12 months following the initial 12-month exclusion, the responsible entity must exclude at least 50 percent of any increase in income of the family member as a result of employment over the family member's baseline income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This phase-in reduces the exclusion to at least 50% in the second year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum 2-year (24-month) lifetime limit for disallowance
rubrics_metrics.description: The disallowance provided under paragraphs (c)(1) and (c)(2) is limited to a lifetime 24-month period: up to 12 months for the initial exclusion and up to 12 months for the second-year phase-in, counted from the initial exclusion start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible entities must track lifetime usage of the disallowance per individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grandfathering/Effect of regulatory changes on currently participating families
rubrics_metrics.description: Families participating in the disallowance prior to May 9, 2016 continue to be governed by the section as it existed immediately prior to that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies transitional rule for families enrolled before regulatory amendment date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallowance not applicable to admissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The disallowance of increases in income for persons with disabilities does not apply for purposes of admission to the program (income eligibility determinations or income targeting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used only for ongoing participants' income calculations, not to determine initial eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal limitation and sunset for disallowance provision
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies to families receiving the disallowance on December 31, 2023 and the section will lapse on January 1, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation includes explicit sunset and applicability dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net assets and property ownership restrictions on assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: A dwelling in public housing may not be rented, and Section 8 assistance may not be provided initially or upon reexamination, if (i) the family's net assets exceed $100,000 (adjusted annually by CPI-W), or (ii) the family has present ownership interest/right to reside in and authority to sell real property suitable for occupancy by the family, subject to exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The $100,000 threshold is adjusted annually; owners/PHAs must check net asset definition at §5.603.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to real property disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Real property restriction does not apply to: (A) property for which family receives assistance under 24 CFR 982.620 or Homeownership Option in 24 CFR part 982; (B) property jointly owned with non-household member who resides at that jointly owned property; (C) victims of domestic violence/dating violence/sexual assault/stalking (as defined in Subpart L); (D) family offering property for sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHA/owner must recognize listed statutory exceptions when applying property-ownership restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for 'suitable for occupancy' exception to property restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: A property is considered suitable for occupancy unless family demonstrates it: (i) does not meet disability-related needs (e.g., accessibility, extra bedrooms); (ii) is not sufficient for family size; (iii) is geographically a hardship (distance/commute to work or school); (iv) is not safe to reside in due to physical condition that cannot be easily remedied; or (v) is not a property the family may reside in under State/local laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Family bears burden of demonstrating one of these conditions to avoid disqualification based on ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable documentation and confidentiality for asset/property verification
rubrics_metrics.description: PHA/owner may determine net assets based on a family certification that net assets do not exceed $50,000 (adjusted annually by CPI-W) without further verification; similarly may rely on family certification of no present ownership interest in real property. For exceptions based on victim status, PHA/owner must comply with confidentiality requirements of §5.2007 and accept self-certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification must state expected income from assets which must be included in family's income; confidentiality protections limit documentation requests for victims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement discretion and exceptions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When recertifying income, a PHA or owner may choose not to enforce the net asset/property restrictions or may establish exceptions, but only pursuant to a policy adopted by the PHA/owner; eligibility criteria for exceptions may vary by family type and factors (age, disability, income, ability to find alternative housing, supportive services) and must conform to fair housing laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs/owners must adopt written policy and ensure compliance with nondiscrimination requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay of eviction/termination based on asset restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The PHA or owner may delay for up to 6 months the initiation of eviction or termination proceedings of a family based on noncompliance with the asset/property restrictions, unless doing so conflicts with other law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides short-term delay authority to avoid immediate removal for asset-based noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of asset restrictions to programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The restrictions on assistance based on net assets and property ownership apply to Section 8 (tenant-based and project-based) and public housing programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies program coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total tenant payment (TTP) calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Total tenant payment is the highest of: (1) 30 percent of the family's monthly adjusted income; (2) 10 percent of the family's monthly income; (3) for families receiving welfare payments designated for housing, the portion so designated adjusted to actual housing costs; (4) the minimum rent per §5.630; or (5) for public housing only, the alternative non-public housing rent per §960.102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TTP is rounded to nearest dollar; if welfare assistance is ratably reduced from the standard of need by a percentage, the amount under (3) uses one application of the percentage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum rent amount limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The PHA must charge no less than a minimum monthly rent established by the responsible entity except as provided; for public housing and section 8 moderate rehabilitation or voucher programs, minimum rent may be up to $50; for other section 8 programs, minimum rent is $25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs may set the minimum up to statutory caps; responsible entity establishes exact amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial hardship exemption from minimum rent — qualifying circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: A family is exempt from minimum rent if unable to pay because of financial hardship, which includes: (i) loss of or awaiting eligibility determination for Federal/State/local assistance (including certain lawfully admitted noncitizens affected by PRWORA), (ii) risk of eviction for inability to pay minimum rent, (iii) income decrease because of changed circumstances including job loss, (iv) death in the family, or (v) other circumstances determined by responsible entity or HUD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible entity's written policies define financial hardship and may include additional circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure upon family request for hardship exemption — suspension and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon family request, the responsible entity must suspend the minimum rent beginning the month following the request until it determines whether a qualifying hardship exists and whether it is temporary or long term; the entity must promptly determine hardship status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For public housing, PHA must suspend and may not evict for nonpayment of minimum rent during the 90-day period beginning the month following request; if temporary hardship, PHA reinstates minimum rent from start of suspension and offers reasonable repayment agreement for back minimum rent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardship exemption rules for all Section 8 programs
rubrics_metrics.description: For all Section 8 programs, responsible entity must suspend minimum rent beginning the month following request until determination; if hardship is temporary, must not impose minimum rent during 90-day suspension and must offer reasonable repayment agreement for back rent; if no qualifying hardship, must reinstate minimum rent including back rent from start of suspension on terms determined by entity; if hardship is long term, must exempt family from minimum rent for duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemption applies only to payment of minimum rent and not to other TTP elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public housing grievance hearing on hardship denial — no escrow deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: If a public housing family requests a hearing under the PHA grievance procedure to review denial or limitation of a financial hardship exemption, the family is not required to pay any escrow deposit to obtain a grievance hearing on such issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects right to administrative hearing without escrow requirement for hardship disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility reimbursement applicability and payment threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility reimbursement rules apply to Section 8 programs other than the voucher program (voucher program utility reimbursement per §982.514(b)) and to public housing families paying income-based rent. Responsible entity pays a utility reimbursement if the utility allowance exceeds the total tenant payment; it may make payments not less than once per calendar-quarter for reimbursements totaling $45 or less per quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If family leaves before next quarterly reimbursement, responsible entity must reimburse prorated share; PHAs/owners using quarterly option must have hardship policies for tenants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility reimbursement payment recipient and notification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In public housing (income-based rent), Section 8 moderate rehabilitation, and Section 8 voucher programs, PHA may pay utility reimbursement to family or directly to utility supplier; if paying supplier, PHA must notify family of amount paid. In other Section 8 programs, owner must pay either to the family or, with family consent, to the utility supplier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/PHAs must obtain consent when paying supplier in owner-covered programs and must inform families when supplier payment is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenant rent calculation for Section 8 programs and public housing
rubrics_metrics.description: For Section 8 programs other than the Section 8 voucher program, tenant rent is total tenant payment minus any utility allowance. Public housing tenant rent is determined under §960.253.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tenant rent depends on program-specific rules and relevant cross-referenced sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 8 project-based assistance eligibility and income-targeting applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets requirements concerning income-eligibility and income-targeting for Section 8 project-based assistance programs, except moderate rehabilitation and project-based voucher programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies program scope and cross-references exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic eligibility — family definition and income eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must meet all eligibility requirements to receive assistance, must be a family as defined in §5.403, and must be income-eligible; eligible applicants include single persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners must verify family status and income-eligibility per definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low income limit for admission to project-based assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: No family other than a low income family is eligible for admission to Section 8 project-based assistance programs (this does not apply to project-based voucher program under part 983).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission policies must enforce low-income eligibility except where specifically exempted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting requirement to extremely low income families
rubrics_metrics.description: For each assisted project, of the dwelling units that become available for occupancy in any fiscal year under the contract, not less than 40 percent shall be available for leasing only by extremely low income families at time of admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners must reserve at least 40% of newly available assisted units each fiscal year for ELI families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on admission of low income but not very low income families (percent caps)
rubrics_metrics.description: For units available before Oct 1, 1981: not more than 25% of such Section 8 project-based units leased on/after that date may be to low income families other than very low income families. For units available on/after Oct 1, 1981: not more than 15% of such units initially becoming available may be leased to low income families other than very low income families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner may only lease such units to very low income families except with HUD prior approval per paragraphs (d)(3) and (d)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for exception to admission limitations — required basis and supporting data
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner requesting approval to admit low income families other than very low income families must state the basis for the exception and provide supporting data. Bases HUD may consider include need to preserve financial viability due to insufficient ELI applicants, commitment to broad income range, state HFA policy evidence, projects financed under certain statutes, or displacement considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner's request must articulate and document specific reasons; HUD considers enumerated bases among others.

rubrics_metrics.name: HUD discretion and review of exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to grant an exception is committed to HUD's discretion; HUD will review exceptions granted to owners at regular intervals and may withdraw permission if exceptions are not being used or after periodic review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No entitlement implied by listing grounds; owners should not assume automatic approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income used for eligibility and targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Family annual income as defined in §5.609 is used for both income-eligibility and income-targeting under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners must use the §5.609 annual income definition in determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting obligations for Section 8 owners
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 8 owners must comply with HUD-prescribed reporting requirements, including income reporting to permit HUD to monitor compliance with income-eligibility and targeting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners should maintain records and submit data as required by HUD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner selection function subject to income-targeting and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection for occupancy of a project or unit is the owner's function but is subject to income-eligibility and income-targeting requirements in §5.653(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner selection policies must not contravene HUD income-targeting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenant selection plan requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner must adopt a written tenant selection plan in accordance with HUD requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan must be written and conform to HUD-prescribed content and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on ordering selection to favor higher-income families
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner may not select a family in an order different from the owner's waiting list for the purpose of selecting a relatively higher income family, but may select based on income to satisfy targeting requirements of §5.653(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners may not manipulate waiting lists to prefer higher-income applicants except to meet HUD targeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching family characteristics to unit features and accessibility priority
rubrics_metrics.description: In selecting a family for a particular unit, the owner may match family characteristics (e.g., bedrooms) to the unit, and must first offer units with special accessibility features to families including persons with disabilities who require such features (see §§8.27 and 100.202).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accessibility needs take priority when assigning specially equipped units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bedroom-size limitation for single non-elderly/non-disabled/non-displaced persons
rubrics_metrics.description: A single person who is not elderly, displaced, a person with disabilities, or the remaining member of a resident family may not be provided a housing unit with two or more bedrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits household composition to unit size in specified circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner must inform applicants of available preferences and allow qualification showing
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner must inform all applicants about available preferences and must give applicants an opportunity to show that they qualify for available preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency and applicant opportunity to claim preferences are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency preference rules, approval, and nondiscrimination limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Residency preferences (preference for persons residing in a specified geographic area) are not prohibited but must comply with nondiscrimination and equal opportunity requirements. An owner's residency preference must be approved by HUD via (A) prior approval of housing market area in AFFH marketing plan; (B) prior approval in the PHA plan of the jurisdiction; or (C) modification of Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing Plan. Residency preferences must not have purpose/effect of delaying or denying admission based on protected characteristics, must not be based on how long an applicant has resided/worked in area, and applicants working or hired in the area and graduates/participants of job-prep programs may be treated as residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict HUD approval and nondiscrimination constraints apply to residency preferences; specific approval routes listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working family preference limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner may adopt a preference for admission of working families; an applicant is given the benefit of the working family preference if head/spouse/sole member is age 62+ or a person with disabilities; owner must not base preference on amount of earned income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference is based on employment status, not magnitude of earnings; elderly/PwD protections apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for families including persons with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner may adopt a preference for admission of families that include a person with disabilities but may not adopt a preference for persons with a specific disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad disability-based preference allowed, but singling out particular disabilities is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for victims of domestic violence — consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner should consider whether to adopt a preference for admission of families that include victims of domestic violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption is discretionary but recommended for owners to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for certain single persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner may adopt a preference for admission of single persons who are age 62 or older, displaced, homeless, or persons with disabilities over other single persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows prioritization among single-person applicants with specific vulnerabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular reexamination requirement for Section 8 project-based programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner must conduct a reexamination and redetermination of family income and composition at least annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual certifications are mandated to maintain correct rent/subsidy calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim reexamination upon family request or owner awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Family may request an interim reexamination because of any changes since last examination; owner must conduct any interim reexamination within a reasonable time after request or when owner becomes aware of an increase in adjusted income. 'Reasonable time' generally should not exceed 30 days from date family reports changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness standard tied to verification complexity but generally <=30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner discretion to decline interim reexamination for small decreases
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner may decline to conduct an interim reexamination for decreases if it estimates the family's adjusted income will decrease by less than ten percent of the family's annual adjusted income (or a lower HUD-established or owner-established threshold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners may set lower thresholds; must document policy consistently with §(c)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory interim reexamination for increases of estimated 10% or more and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner must conduct an interim reexamination when aware that family's adjusted income has changed by an amount estimated to result in an increase of ten percent or more in annual adjusted income, except (i) owner may not consider increases in earned income when estimating/calculating unless family previously received an interim reduction during the certification period; and (ii) owner may choose not to conduct an interim reexamination in the last three months of a certification period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earned income increases excluded from triggering interim increases unless prior interim reduction occurred; last-quarter discretion allows administrative efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner policies on reporting changes in income/composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner must adopt policies consistent with interim reexamination rules prescribing when and under what conditions the family must report changes in income or composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written reporting policies must be consistent with the regulatory thresholds and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date rules for rent changes after reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If family reports change timely per owner's policies, owner must provide 30 days advance notice of any rent increase which will be effective the first day of the month after the 30-day notice; rent decreases effective first day of first month after date of actual change. If family failed to report timely, owners implement resulting rent increases retroactively to the first of the month following the date of change; rent decreases implemented no later than the first rent period following completion of reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely reporting benefits families by delaying retroactive increases and accelerating decreases; owners must follow specified notice and effective-date rules.
